verdict.rationale: Intel's spec page documents the boost ceiling ('up to 5.70 GHz') and the 36M cache. Independent reviews corroborate strong productivity and multi-core results: faster than the 14900K and roughly matching the 9950X score. Phoronix, however, saw compiler segfaults with DDR5-8000/6000 memory that went away at the rated DDR5-6400. missing for 10: documented core/thread counts, detailed boost behavior beyond the max frequency, dedicated compile-time benchmark figures, and stability without memory-speed caveats.

support.subject: As a developer, I can compile big codebases and run heavy parallel jobs fast — documented core counts and boost behavior, corroborated by independent multi-core benchmarks

citations.quote: Intel's Core Ultra 9 285K makes strong gains in productivity workloads
Compared to its predecessor, 14900K, it ends up both faster (barring some outliers) and significantly more power efficient.
So, very, very similar to the 9950X score (100.x%)
But when switching to DDR5-6400 DIMMs as the rated memory speed for the Core Ultra 200S, everything was behaving great.
